reader_notes: Reads exactly like a long-form trade-press feature; the chemistry (volatile phenols from lignin, glycosylation inside the berry, saliva releasing the phenol retronasally, slow acid hydrolysis in bottle) is coherent and internally consistent throughout.

q4 asked me to weigh 'backs the panel outright' against 'sets the two positions side by side'. The sentence 'She is right about that', followed by 'The January readings were unremarkable and the January wines were not', settles it - but 'outright' is a strong word for a writer who elsewhere reports both sides neutrally, so this was the slowest question of the five.

Minor stumble in paragraph 1: 'It made no difference' immediately followed by 'One washed lot even read a little higher' momentarily reads as a self-contradiction until the 'will not build on a single pair' hedge lands.
Heavy lexical load for an exam text (veraison and glycoside are glossed; 'particulate load', 'fermenter', 'bound/free' are not), but nothing that blocked comprehension.
